**Course Description:**

Modern computer network analysis and design using a structured approach based on the implementation of the ISO/OSI model and current standardized protocols. Network architectural layers above the physical layer - only a brief overview is presented on the physical layer.

**Prerequisites:** CEC 320.

**Supplemental Text:**

-   Computer Networking: A Top-Down Approach, by Jim Kurose with Keith Ross, Pearson

**Course Objectives:**

The purpose of the course is to:

-   Understand the different layers of the ISO/OSI model and what each layer deals with.

-   Analyze and evaluate network architectures by applying the ISO/OSI model, focusing on the functionalities and interactions of network layers above the physical layer.

-   Design and optimize network solutions using a structured approach that integrates current industry standards and best practices

-   Understand different transmission types and the characteristics of each

**Learning Outcomes**

Upon completion of this course, students should be able to:

-   Understand the different layers in the ISO/OSI model.

-   Analyze information captured from several layers.

-   Use programs to capture transmission data.

-   Understand the different security flaws for each layer.

**Grading**:

Students will receive grade points on assignments, examinations, a course project. Each student's final course grade will be determined by a weighted sum of grade points received during the course. The relative weight of each grading element in the final grade will be computed as follows:

Assignments 30%

Class Participation 10%

Quizzes 10%

Examinations: 30%

Final Report 20%

The course letter grade is awarded as follows:

**A** 100 -- 90

**B** 89 -- 80

**C** 79 -- 70

**D** 69 -- 60

**F** less than 60

**Course Policies:**

The examinations will be roughly equally spaced through the term and will emphasize material covered since the previous examination. Resources outside of the required textbook may be posted in Canvas or discussed in-class.

Attendance is not mandatory. However, students are highly encouraged to attend all class sessions to benefit from the in-class discussions and interactions. If a student does not attend a class, it is the student's responsibility to ensure that they determine what occurred during the class, including any of the instructor's announcements concerning assignments and due dates.

Students may be excused from deadlines or examinations only in the event of a medical or personal emergency sanctioned by the University Office of Judicial Affairs. Makeup of any examination excused on such a basis must be arranged with the instructor.

Work submitted late will be penalized by deducting a letter grade per every 24-hour period past the due date up to a 50 grade, after this threshold the late penalty is not assessed. Work not submitted will count as 0.
